title: Stalk normalization compared with normalization of its generic torsor
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral Noetherian quasi-separated scheme and $c:C\to S$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated smooth morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $q:C_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec}k(S)$ and $j:C_\eta\to C$ exhibit the generic fibre, and let $Z\to C_\eta$ be a finite etale $G$-torsor [def-pc-fibre-product, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let $U\subseteq S$ contain $\eta$ and let $P\to C_U$ be finite etale. Suppose $j_U:C_\eta\to C_U$ and $\psi:Z\to P$ exhibit a cartesian comparison, with $i_Uj_U=j$. Let $s\notin U$ satisfy: every $t$ specializing to $s$ and outside $U$ equals $s$. Suppose $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is a discrete valuation ring (a nonfield local principal ideal domain). Set $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$, $L=C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A$, $d:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, $K=k(S)$ with its canonical fraction-field $A$-algebra structure, $b:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $L_K=L\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $N$ be the concrete relative normalization of $P\to C_U\to C$ [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization], and $n:N\times_C L\to L$ its pullback. There exists a finite etale $G$-torsor $W\to L_K$ and an isomorphism $\beta:N\times_C L\cong p.\mathrm{normalization}$, where $p:W\to L$ is the composite with $L_K\to L$, such that $\beta$ commutes with the structure maps to $L$. No assumption on invertibility of $|G|$, and no finiteness assumption on $n$, is made.

proof.text:
Put A = O_{S,s} and K = k(S), which is a fraction field of A. The map Spec A
has image the generalizations of s. Minimality of s outside U says all its other points
lie in U. A DVR has only its generic and closed points, so the inverse image of U is
exactly Spec K. Pulling back the given generic-fibre square identifies the generic
fibre of L = C times_S Spec A with the base change of C_eta. Pull back Z and its action
along this identification: its total space is the fibre product, and each action map
is induced by the action on Z and the identity on the new base. Finiteness, etaleness,
surjectivity and the simply transitive action identity are preserved by base change.
This constructs W. The comparison square hψ identifies W with the restriction to the
punctured local base of PA. Choose an affine neighbourhood V = Spec B of s in S,
and cover c⁻¹(V) by affine opens E = Spec R. If the prime of s in B is q, the
corresponding base change of E has ring R localized at the image of B \ q.
The inverse image of E in PA is qcqs: PA is finite over C_U and C_U is a
quasi-compact open of C. Its sections therefore commute with this flat localization
base change. Relative normalization on E is the spectrum of the integral closure
of R in these sections. Tag 0307 identifies its localization with the integral
closure for the generic cover W. The affine comparison isomorphisms preserve the
algebra maps from the base and agree on intersections by the universal property of
relative normalization (035I). Gluing them gives β with the asserted equality over L.
This works also for an empty total space. Invertibility of the group order and
ramification theory are not used in this comparison.
